ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle ACB = 90^\circ$, $AC = BC$. A straight line DE is drawn outside $\triangle ABC$ through point C, and perpendicular lines are drawn from points A and B to line DE, with the feet of the perpendiculars being E and D, respectively. If $AE=4$ and $BD=3$, then what is the length of $DE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that $\angle ACB=90^\circ$, \\
it follows that $\angle ACE + \angle BCD = 90^\circ$.\\
Since $\angle ACE + \angle CAE = 90^\circ$,\\
it implies that $\angle BCD = \angle CAE$.\\
In $\triangle ACE$ and $\triangle CBD$, \\
$\begin{array}{c}
\angle CAE = \angle BCD,\\
\angle E = \angle D = 90^\circ,\\
AC = BC,
\end{array}$\\
hence, $\triangle ACE \cong \triangle CBD$ by AAS,\\
thus, CE = BD = 3, CD = AE = 4,\\
therefore, DE = CE + CD = \boxed{7}.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the diagram, E, C, and D lie on the same straight segment with C between E and D. Point A is below E and point B is below D. Segment AE is drawn from A to the line DE, and segment BD is drawn from B to the line DE; these are the perpendicular drops described in the problem. Segments AC and BC form triangle ABC, with C at the top on DE and AB at the bottom. Reasoning: Since C lies on line DE and ∠ACB = 90°, the two angles adjacent to ∠ACB along the straight line DE satisfy ∠ACE + ∠BCD = 90°. In right triangle ACE, because AE ⟂ DE and CE lies on DE, ∠E = 90°, so ∠ACE + ∠CAE = 90°. Therefore ∠BCD = ∠CAE. Now compare triangles ACE and CBD: ∠E = ∠D = 90°, ∠CAE = ∠BCD, and AC = BC. Thus triangle ACE is congruent to triangle CBD. Corresponding sides give CE = BD = 3 and CD = AE = 4. Since C is between E and D, DE = CE + CD = 3 + 4 = 7.
